research_question: Does a finite simple outerplanar graph of maximum degree at most four admit an acyclic 4-edge-coloring?

mathematical_conditions.exposed_pair_condition: each pair contains exactly one color incident to s and exactly one color incident to t
mathematical_conditions.dominance_comparison: same ordered terminal masks A,B; retain inclusion-minimal exposed pair masks F

reproducibility_config.graph_atlas_predicate: at least one edge, max_degree<=4, outerplanar (universal apex planarity test)
reproducibility_config.maximal_construction: zigzag polygon triangulation of size n
reproducibility_config.nonmaximal_construction: randomly delete nonbridge edges from zigzag triangulation
reproducibility_config.component_decomposition: NetworkX biconnected_component_edges then virtual-edge two-terminal SP reductions
reproducibility_config.statistic: median of 7 per graph and unweighted mean across 60 sampled graphs per order
reproducibility_config.timing_scope: DP-only run_tree measured using perf_counter_ns; exclude decomposition, memory and verification
reproducibility_config.memory_scope: separate tracemalloc peak, NOT process RSS
reproducibility_config.certificate_check: all adjacent edge colors differ and all two-color induced subgraphs are forests

figure8_visual_transcription.color_witness: independently reconstructed; may not match printed per-edge colors

source_provenance.statement_of_limits: The 17-page paper describes an i9 laptop, but the stored execution manifest has no independent CPU/RAM hardware evidence; raw archived timing values are not portable.
source_provenance.figure8: topology manually transcribed from labeled PDF, witness separately computed; not recovered original edge/slot source
